newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: U.S. dollar stocks dominate Singapore market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. dollar stocks dominate Singapore market.

text.p: Small-capitalised stocks denominated in U.S. dollars dominated activity on the Singapore stock market on Friday as the local currency slipped to new 30-month lows, dealers said.
"Currency ruled. You can see the top volumes are generated by U.S. dollar-denominated stocks and small-capitalised stocks, some of which are laggards," said a dealer with a local house.

On Friday, the Singapore dollar fell below 1.4665 to the U.S. currency as funds continued to buy the U.S. dollar. Currency dealers also said the local currency was adjusting to recent weakness in other regional currencies.
U.S. dollar-listed CM Telecom, Roly, Thakral and Huan Hsin were among the actives which hit new highs.
The Straits Times Industrials index ended 3.69 points up at 1,924.23, underpinned by a 10 cent gain in car distributor Cycle & Carriage to Singapore $12.60.
Indonesian Sinar Mas Tunggal's rescue vehicle of Amcol, Asia Food & Properties, ended at US$1.16 after hitting a high of US$1.44. It led the actives, with over 37 million shares traded.
Multimedia Creative Technology ended 40 cents down at S$32.40, reflecting Thursday's correction in U.S. technology stocks on Nasdaq.
Dealers said the market awaited clearer market direction from Singapore's June non-oil export figures, due for release on Monday. Most were expecting an improvement.
